note: Friday 07:00 SGT, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Thu 30 Jul US close. The dominant shifts: (1) a sharp RELIEF RALLY reversed Wednesday's hawkish-hold selloff — Nasdaq +2.8% (best day of the year), S&P +1.7% to a record 7,437.63 — as Amazon's AWS +37% blowout and Microsoft's record one-day gain re-validated AI-capex; (2) 'stagflation-lite' data (Q2 GDP +1.5%, core PCE sticky +3.3%) kept the Fed hawkish (10Y ~4.68%); (3) gold pushed to ~$4,080 near a record and oil held >$92 as the US-Iran pause stayed broken. 8 of 12 items are dated Wed 29-Thu 30 Jul (last 24-48h). Every item source-verified.

items.headline: Stocks snap back hard: Nasdaq +2.8% (best day of year), S&P +1.7% to record 7,437.63, Dow +1.2%
items.summary: US equities staged a sharp relief rally the day after the hawkish-hold selloff, reversing most of Wednesday's drop. The Nasdaq Composite jumped 2.8% to 25,122.18, ending a six-day losing streak; the S&P 500 rose 1.7% to a record ~7,437.63 and the Dow gained 613.92 points (+1.2%) to 52,208.06. Microsoft posted its largest one-day market-value gain on record and semiconductors rebounded as AI-capex fears eased. The VIX fell back toward ~18 from Wednesday's ~20.66 spike.
items.actionable: The AI-capex-doubt scare that had pressured the SMIC/HK-tech chip leg reversed — a relief for the tech-beta parts of the book, but the S&P at a fresh record with sticky 3.3% core PCE leaves little valuation cushion. Don't chase the record; keep the USD cash pile as dry powder and let next week's SGX/HK earnings and the 31 Jul Flow Show confirm the risk-on turn before redeploying.

items.headline: Gold pushes to ~$4,080 near a record; silver holds ~$57 on the sticky-inflation/haven bid
items.summary: Gold climbed ~0.4% to around $4,080/oz on Thursday, near a record, as sticky June core PCE (+3.3% y/y), the oil spike and the reignited US-Iran conflict drew a haven and inflation-hedge bid — even as equities rallied and the dollar eased to DXY ~100.8. Silver held around $57/oz and copper firmed to ~$6.44/lb. Gold funds took their largest weekly inflow since April; the structural silver-deficit thesis (Silver Institute 6th straight annual deficit) is intact.
items.actionable: The book's core firmed even into a risk-on equity tape — gold near a record is the cleanest hold and the steadier hedge against the reignited Iran risk and sticky inflation; favor gold-heavy GDX over pure silver leverage while the higher-for-longer Fed keeps real rates a two-sided pull on silver. Hold the core; hedge the silver-vs-gold spread rather than adding leverage into the record.

items.headline: Amazon jumps ~9% AH on AWS +37% blowout; raises 2026 capex to ~$220B — AI-capex re-validated
items.summary: Amazon rose more than 9% after hours on a Q2 beat led by AWS, which grew 37% year-over-year to $42.23B — its fastest in 18 quarters and well above the ~31% consensus — with AI and custom-chip units each running above a $25B run-rate. North America revenue rose 16% to $116.2B on Prime Day, and the company raised its 2026 capex plan to ~$220B. The result directly reversed the AI-overcapacity narrative that had wiped >$1trn from semis the prior week.
items.actionable: The AWS +37% blowout and raised capex re-validate the AI-infrastructure spend that the semis rout had doubted — a positive read-through to the SMIC chip leg and the whole AI-hardware complex. It argues the internet/platform layer AND the chip layer both benefit when hyperscaler capex re-accelerates; keep Tencent/Xiaomi favored but the acute bear case on the chip leg has eased.

items.headline: Q2 GDP slows to +1.5%, core PCE sticky at +3.3% — 'stagflation-lite' keeps the Fed hawkish
items.summary: The advance Q2 GDP print came in at +1.5% annualized, down from +2.1% in Q1 and below expectations — a clear growth slowdown. June headline PCE rose +3.7% y/y and core PCE stayed sticky at +3.3% y/y (in line, prior 3.4%), well above the 2% target. The combination validated the three July FOMC hike dissents and Chair Warsh's hawkish framing: the 10Y rose ~10bp to ~4.68% and the 2Y hit fresh 2026 highs even as equities rallied.
items.actionable: Sticky 3.3% core PCE keeps September a live hike risk — the direct higher-for-longer headwind for levered silver and SGX REITs, with the 10Y at ~4.68%. The sub-trend growth read is a warning for the most cyclical, rate-sensitive parts of the book. Keep the big USD cash pile (~3.5-3.75%) as productive dry powder and hedge the rate-sensitive sleeve rather than adding leverage into it.

items.headline: US-Iran pause stays broken: Brent holds >$92 on renewed US strikes and Hormuz shipping attacks
items.summary: The US-Iran fighting pause remained collapsed on Thursday: a fresh wave of US strikes and Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz kept Brent above ~$92 (WTI ~$84) after Wednesday's +7-8% spike (Brent +7.9% to $90.74, WTI +6.6% to $84.46). The 60-day ceasefire signed the prior month is effectively in shambles, with strikes resuming on both sides and the war/inflation premium re-armed.
items.actionable: Double-edged: the sustained oil premium re-arms the inflation/rate-hike fear pressuring the rate-sensitive book (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech) even as the Fed stays hawkish, but it restores the geopolitical safe-haven bid under gold/silver and lifts the small energy long. Keep gold-heavy GDX as the hedge against the pause staying broken; the Hormuz/Red Sea front is again the key cross-portfolio swing factor.

items.headline: Apple beats on revenue (+16.6%, iPhone +22%) but falls ~4% AH on a Services shortfall
items.summary: Apple's fiscal Q3 revenue came in at $111.18B (+16.6% y/y), topping expectations, with iPhone sales up 22% to $56.99B and Services at a record $30.98B. But shares fell more than 4% after hours in volatile trade as investors flagged a shortfall in Services revenue growth versus the loftiest expectations, overshadowing the otherwise strong hardware quarter.
items.actionable: Idiosyncratic to Apple (a Services-growth miss against a strong iPhone quarter) rather than an AI-capex or macro signal, so limited read-through to the portfolio — the AMZN/MSFT capex re-validation is the more important tech tape. Notable mainly as the one blemish on an otherwise constructive mega-cap earnings gauntlet that powered Thursday's rebound.

items.headline: Fed delivers a HAWKISH hold: 9-3 with three dissents for a hike; Warsh 'won't hesitate' on inflation
items.summary: The FOMC held the target range at 3.50-3.75% for a fifth straight meeting, but the decision read hawkish: the vote was 9-3 with three regional-president dissents preferring an immediate 25bp hike, aggravated by Middle East escalation. Chair Kevin Warsh issued a deliberately short statement, gave no September commitment and framed prices — not the labor market — as the policy driver. Thursday's sticky core PCE (+3.3%) then validated the dissenters; markets now see additional hikes possible later in 2026.
items.actionable: The hawkish hold, now validated by sticky PCE, keeps September a live hike risk and the 10Y at ~4.68% — the direct higher-for-longer headwind for levered silver and SGX REITs. Hedge the rate-sensitive book rather than adding leverage into it; the productive USD cash pile earns ~3.5-3.75% as dry powder for the shakeout.

items.headline: Semis rebound with the tape but Burry adds to his Micron short (24 Jul, at $933.86)
items.summary: Semiconductors bounced on Thursday alongside the AWS/MSFT-led rally after a >$1trn drawdown since 24 Jul, with SMIC's HK line and the broad SOX recovering. But Michael Burry — now publishing on Substack after deregistering Scion — disclosed adding to his Micron short on 24 Jul at $933.86, part of an expanded NVDA/MU/AMAT/SOXX/TSLA/CAT bear book arguing the SOX sits near the top of its 15-year forward-P/E band and AI-capex can't justify valuations. Tepper (Q1 13F) and Congress's Newhouse remain on the memory-bull side.
items.actionable: The AWS capex re-validation eases the acute bear case on the SMIC chip leg near-term, but Burry's fresh, larger Micron short is the standing warning that the group is richly valued into any capex wobble. Continue favoring the internet/consumer HK names (Tencent, Xiaomi) as the core while treating the chip leg as higher-beta and two-sided; size for volatility.

items.headline: Crypto recovers with risk appetite: Bitcoin ~$64.8k, Ether ~$1,923, Solana ~$74.6
items.summary: Crypto firmed on Thursday as risk appetite returned post-Fed: Bitcoin rose to around $64,800, Ether to ~$1,923 and Solana to ~$74.6, tracking the equity relief rally, though the DeFi complex lagged (reportedly -11.5% on the day). The crypto Fear & Greed index sat in the low-30s ('Fear') across providers. With no crypto-specific catalyst, the market continues to trade as a risk-appetite barometer off the macro rate channel.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto is the cleanest read on the risk-appetite impulse — its recovery with equities confirms the rebound was a genuine risk-on turn, not just a mechanical bounce. Treat it as a barometer: a further hawkish repricing into September would pressure both crypto and the metals/REIT rate-sensitivity trade; a dovish data surprise would relieve both.

items.headline: SGX earnings season opens with STI near a record (5,561, +21% TR YTD); banks upgraded to Overweight
items.summary: Singapore shares sit near record territory — the STI printed ~5,561.42 on 15 Jul (+21.2% total return YTD) — as the earnings season opens: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT reports 5 Aug, DBS 6 Aug, and OCBC/UOB 7 Aug. SG banks were upgraded to Overweight by several houses on resilient NIMs and capital returns, while the S-REIT sleeve navigates the higher-for-longer rate backdrop; Keppel DC REIT earlier posted 1H26 DPU +11.3%.
items.actionable: A constructive backdrop for the SGX banks/REIT sleeve into next week's prints, but the hawkish Fed (10Y ~4.68%) and the oil-spike inflation risk are fresh headwinds for the rate-sensitive S-REITs. Watch DBS results 6 Aug (guided FY26 slightly lower) and CapLand Ascendas REIT 5 Aug; the banks are the more insulated leg vs the REITs into a higher-for-longer path.

items.headline: China rare-earth enforcement tightens; MP/USAR on control list, 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff nears
items.summary: China's rare-earth grip tightened: MOFCOM Announcement No. 26 (a reporting-and-reward enforcement regime) took effect 1 Jul, and export curbs were extended to 14 EU firms on 24 Jul, while MP Materials and USA Rare Earth remain on China's entity-specific dual-use control list (added 22 Jun). The broad October-2025 MOFCOM export controls stay SUSPENDED only until 10 Nov 2026 (~3.5 months out). Lynas has advanced ex-China heavy-REE production and DoD-backed Western supply continues to build.
items.actionable: Structural Western-supply validation for the ex-China rare-earth watchlist (Lynas heavy-REE, MP's DoD backing, UUUU's build-out), but the 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff is the calendar catalyst: near-term pricing urgency stays eased, so accumulate MP/UUUU on weakness into a potential control snap-back rather than chase the strategic re-rate now.

items.headline: Tencent pauses buyback into results blackout and cuts its Kuaishou stake below 'substantial' (to 9.37%)
items.summary: Tencent ran near-daily buybacks through early July (e.g. ~1.065M shares/HK$500.7M on 9 Jul) under its 10% AGM mandate, then PAUSED the program into the customary blackout ahead of its 12 August interim results. Separately, an HKEXnews notice (dated ~6 Jul) showed Tencent disposing of Kuaishou (1024) shares, cutting its stake from ~15.68% to ~9.37% and ceasing to be a substantial shareholder. Xiaomi's own buyback continued (3.9M shares/HK$100.7M, 15 Jul).
items.actionable: The buyback blackout temporarily lifts a mechanical support under Tencent into its 12 Aug print — a reason not to add aggressively before results, even as the internet sleeve stays the preferred HK-tech core over the SMIC chip leg. The Kuaishou trim is capital recycling, not a read on Tencent's own franchise. Watch the 12 Aug earnings (buyback resumes after) as the next catalyst.
